### Town histories (as a record substitute)
- Nineteenth-century Vermont town histories, mostly published 1860–1900, reprint colonial-era proprietors' records that are otherwise difficult to access (FamilySearch Wiki, "Vermont Genealogy," https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Vermont_Genealogy). For the pre-statehood period, these published histories may be the most practical substitute for lost or scattered original proprietors' records.

### Church records, census records, probate, court, military, cemetery, newspaper, tax, and other record types
- No tool result in this survey (`collections_search`, `volume_search`, `catalog_search`, `wiki_read` on a constructed Vermont_Vital_Records URL) returned Vermont-specific, period-specific content for these record types. The constructed `Vermont_Vital_Records` URL resolved to a generic, jurisdiction-agnostic "Genealogy Records" page rather than a Vermont-specific article, so no Vermont-specific claims about church, probate, court, or other record series for this period can be sourced here. Note generically from that page only that federal decennial census enumeration begins in 1790 — effectively at the tail end, not within, this pre-1791 target period — and that probate/court records are normally filed at the county or district level, which did not apply uniformly in Vermont until county government was organized after statehood.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Vermont town clerk offices | Early town vital records (some from the 1770s) | In-person or written request directly to the town |
| Vermont State Archives (not independently confirmed by tool results; named generically only) | Presumed custodian of state-level materials | Not confirmed in this survey — contact directly |

## Records NOT online
- The Vermont 1771 Grant Survey Schedule's physical/digital holding location was not identified by any tool in this survey.
- Pre-1857 town clerk vital records are described by the FamilySearch Wiki as surviving "unevenly," with no online aggregation confirmed — consult town clerks directly.
- Church records, probate, court, and tax records for pre-statehood Vermont returned no FamilySearch collection, volume, or catalog hits in this survey.

## Known record losses
- No tool result in this survey specifically confirms a record loss (e.g., fire, war destruction) for pre-statehood Vermont records. Given the disputed New York/New Hampshire jurisdiction and informal governance of the era, uneven survival is noted by the Wiki, but this is different from a documented destruction event — none was found. Treat any apparent absence as a coverage gap in this survey, not a confirmed loss.

## Research tips
- Because Vermont's territory was claimed by both New York and New Hampshire before and during the Republic period, search for pre-1791 records under all three jurisdictional names — this is directly tied to how the Vermont 1771 Grant Survey Schedule itself was created under New York colonial authority to adjudicate New Hampshire grants (FamilySearch Wiki, "Vermont Genealogy," https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Vermont_Genealogy).
- Treat the 1857 statewide civil-registration start date as the dividing line: records before that year depend on whichever town clerk's books survive, so identify the specific town your ancestor lived in before searching further (same source).
- Use nineteenth-century Vermont town histories (mostly published 1860–1900) as a practical substitute where original proprietors' records are hard to access, since the Wiki states these histories often reprint that colonial-era material directly (same source).
- This survey's wiki fetches for "getting started," "online records," and "research tips" each returned the same general Vermont article rather than distinct content, and a constructed Vermont_Vital_Records URL resolved only to a generic non-Vermont-specific page — treat Vermont-specific guidance beyond the "Vermont Genealogy" article as unconfirmed, and consult the FamilySearch Wiki directly for any page this survey may have missed.
- Because `collections_search`, `volume_search`, and `catalog_search` all returned zero results for Vermont in this window, plan on physical/archival research (town clerks, local historical societies, the Vermont State Archives) rather than assuming online indexing will surface pre-statehood material.

This guide covers Vermont as a whole for the years before it became a U.S. state in 1791, when it was really disputed frontier territory claimed by both New York and New Hampshire and governed loosely as the independent "Vermont Republic." The clearest surviving record from this era is a 1771 land-grant list of about 1,800 settlers prepared under New York's authority, plus scattered town clerk books (some towns kept their own birth, marriage, and death entries as early as the 1770s) and later-published town histories that reprinted old land records; there was no organized statewide registration of births, marriages, or deaths until 1857, and the tools used for this survey could not confirm any specific online, indexed, or microfilmed Vermont collections for this early period, meaning most research for this window will have to go through town clerks, local historical societies, and physical archives rather than online search.

Here is the locality guide produced for **Yorkshire, England — 1851** (saved to your project as **loc_001**):

---

## Yorkshire, England — Death Records for 1851

### 1. Civil Registration (Best First Stop)
England and Wales began compulsory civil registration of deaths in **1 July 1837**, so by 1851 the system was well established. Every death should appear in the national **General Register Office (GRO) index**.

- **Search free:** [FreeBMD](https://www.freebmd.org.uk) covers GRO death indexes and is the standard starting point.
- **Search on FamilySearch:** The GRO death index is also searchable through FamilySearch's England & Wales collections.
- Once you find the index entry, you can order the **death certificate** directly from the GRO (gro.gov.uk), which gives cause of death, age, address, and the informant's name.

> ⚠️ **Yorkshire sub-region caveat:** Yorkshire's civil registration districts span three historical ridings — West, North, and East. When searching, check for variants filed under the riding or district name rather than "Yorkshire" alone.

---

### 2. Church of England Parish Burial Registers
Many families continued to be buried in their Church of England parish in 1851, and parish registers are a vital cross-check if the civil record is hard to find.

- **Bishop's Transcripts** (annual copies sent to the diocese) can fill gaps when original registers are damaged.
- Yorkshire parish records are largely held at:
  - **Borthwick Institute for Archives** (University of York) — primary repository for the Diocese of York.
  - **West Yorkshire Archive Service** — for parishes in the West Riding.
  - **North Yorkshire County Record Office** — for North Riding parishes.
- Many have been digitised and are searchable through FamilySearch and Ancestry.

---

### 3. The 1851 Census
The census was taken **30 March 1851** — just months into that year. If the death occurred after that date, the census can confirm where the person was living and who was in the household immediately before death. If the death was earlier in 1851, look for the household without that person.

- Searchable on FamilySearch, Ancestry, and FindMyPast.

---

### 4. Nonconformist Burial Registers
Yorkshire had a strong Nonconformist presence (Methodist, Quaker, Baptist, etc.). If the family was not Church of England, check chapel burial registers — many are held at the same county archives listed above, and some are on FamilySearch.

---

### 5. Probate / Wills
If the person had property, a will or administration grant from **1851** would be in the **Prerogative Court of York** records (prior to January 1858, when probate moved to civil courts). These are held physically at the **Borthwick Institute** and are not fully digitised.

---

### Recommended Search Order

| Step | Record | Where to Search |
|------|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | GRO Death Index (civil registration) | FreeBMD · FamilySearch |
| 2 | 1851 Census (context/confirmation) | FamilySearch · Ancestry · FindMyPast |
| 3 | Parish burial register | FamilySearch · Ancestry · Borthwick Institute |
| 4 | Bishop's Transcripts | Borthwick Institute / County Archives |
| 5 | Nonconformist registers (if applicable) | FamilySearch · County Archives |
| 6 | Probate / Wills (if applicable) | Borthwick Institute (physical archive) |

---

The strongest first move is a **FreeBMD search** for the death registration — this will tell you the GRO district, quarter, volume, and page, from which you can order the full certificate. Would you like a research plan built around a specific name?

# Locality Guide: Yorkshire, England (1851)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Yorkshire is an ancient county; place_search returns two historical representations: "Yorkshire, England" (866-1801) and "Yorkshire, England, United Kingdom" (1801-present).
- **County town:** York.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** England, United Kingdom.
- **Population during period:** place_population returned no data for this standardPlace/period in this run - not confirmed by tooling.
- **Administrative structure:** Divided historically into three Ridings - North, East and West Riding - a division reflected in many record collections being filed by Riding rather than by the county as a whole.
- **Religious denominations:** Church of England parishes (bishop's transcripts and parish registers survive countywide) plus non-conformist congregations (separate non-conformist collections exist for Lancashire/neighbouring counties; a Yorkshire-specific non-conformist FamilySearch collection was not confirmed in this run).

## Boundary changes
- No boundary change affecting the 1851 period was confirmed by place_search_all in this run beyond the 1801 jurisdictional-representation change already noted; this is a different-representation marker, not evidence of a territorial split.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Civil registration of births, marriages and deaths in England and Wales is nationally administered (General Register Office); the FamilySearch "England and Wales, Death Registration Index 1837-2007" collection (id 2285341) begins in 1837, consistent with national civil registration covering 1851. The FamilySearch Wiki Vital Records page did not return Yorkshire-specific text in this run to confirm this independently.
- **What exists:** GRO death index entries (name, registration district, quarter/year, volume/page) for 1851 Yorkshire deaths, searchable via FreeBMD (https://www.freebmd.org.uk/search) and FamilySearch's death registration index.
- **Where held:** Indexes online (FreeBMD, FamilySearch, findmypast, Ancestry); the underlying GRO certificates must be ordered from the General Register Office.
- **Gaps:** The index gives no cause of death or informant detail - only the certificate does.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Church of England parishes throughout Yorkshire.
- **Record types:** Burials (from parish registers) can corroborate or substitute for a civil death record, especially if the GRO index entry cannot be matched with confidence.
- **Where held:** "England, Yorkshire, Parish Registers, 1538-2016" (FamilySearch id 4439317) and "England, Yorkshire, Bishop's Transcripts, 1547-1957" (id 4319956); externally, Ancestry holds "West Yorkshire, England, Church of England Deaths and Burials, 1813-1985" and "North Yorkshire, England, Church of England Deaths and Burials, 1813-1995".
- **Language:** English.

### Census records
- **National census:** "England and Wales, Census, 1851" (FamilySearch id 2563939, 1,569,726 persons indexed) directly covers the target year and can place the person and household shortly before or after a death.
- **Access:** Indexed on FamilySearch; also on Ancestry and findmypast per external_links_search results.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills and administrations.
- **Testate or intestate:** Determines whether to search will or administration records - not yet established for this research subject.
- **Date range / jurisdiction note:** For an 1851 death, probate pre-dates the 1858 national probate system (FamilySearch "England and Wales, National Index of Wills and Administrations, 1858-1957", id 2451051, starts in 1858). Before 1858, Yorkshire probate was handled by ecclesiastical courts (the Prerogative and Exchequer Courts of York); external_links_search returned the Borthwick Institute for Archives, University of York (https://www.york.ac.uk/borthwick/) and Ancestry's "Yorkshire, England, Probate Records, 1521-1858" (collection 5246) and "York Peculiars Probate Index 1383-1883" (findmypast) as relevant holdings.

entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Yorkshire, England (1851)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Yorkshire is an ancient county; place_search returns two historical representations: "Yorkshire, England" (866-1801) and "Yorkshire, England, United Kingdom" (1801-present).
- **County town:** York.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** England, United Kingdom.
- **Population during period:** place_population returned no data for this standardPlace/period in this run - not confirmed by tooling.
- **Administrative structure:** Divided historically into three Ridings - North, East and West Riding - a division reflected in many record collections being filed by Riding rather than by the county as a whole.
- **Religious denominations:** Church of England parishes (bishop's transcripts and parish registers survive countywide) plus non-conformist congregations (separate non-conformist collections exist for Lancashire/neighbouring counties; a Yorkshire-specific non-conformist FamilySearch collection was not confirmed in this run).

## Boundary changes
- No boundary change affecting the 1851 period was confirmed by place_search_all in this run beyond the 1801 jurisdictional-representation change already noted; this is a different-representation marker, not evidence of a territorial split.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Civil registration of births, marriages and deaths in England and Wales is nationally administered (General Register Office); the FamilySearch "England and Wales, Death Registration Index 1837-2007" collection (id 2285341) begins in 1837, consistent with national civil registration covering 1851. The FamilySearch Wiki Vital Records page did not return Yorkshire-specific text in this run to confirm this independently.
- **What exists:** GRO death index entries (name, registration district, quarter/year, volume/page) for 1851 Yorkshire deaths, searchable via FreeBMD (https://www.freebmd.org.uk/search) and FamilySearch's death registration index.
- **Where held:** Indexes online (FreeBMD, FamilySearch, findmypast, Ancestry); the underlying GRO certificates must be ordered from the General Register Office.
- **Gaps:** The index gives no cause of death or informant detail - only the certificate does.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Church of England parishes throughout Yorkshire.
- **Record types:** Burials (from parish registers) can corroborate or substitute for a civil death record, especially if the GRO index entry cannot be matched with confidence.
- **Where held:** "England, Yorkshire, Parish Registers, 1538-2016" (FamilySearch id 4439317) and "England, Yorkshire, Bishop's Transcripts, 1547-1957" (id 4319956); externally, Ancestry holds "West Yorkshire, England, Church of England Deaths and Burials, 1813-1985" and "North Yorkshire, England, Church of England Deaths and Burials, 1813-1995".
- **Language:** English.

### Census records
- **National census:** "England and Wales, Census, 1851" (FamilySearch id 2563939, 1,569,726 persons indexed) directly covers the target year and can place the person and household shortly before or after a death.
- **Access:** Indexed on FamilySearch; also on Ancestry and findmypast per external_links_search results.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills and administrations.
- **Testate or intestate:** Determines whether to search will or administration records - not yet established for this research subject.
- **Date range / jurisdiction note:** For an 1851 death, probate pre-dates the 1858 national probate system (FamilySearch "England and Wales, National Index of Wills and Administrations, 1858-1957", id 2451051, starts in 1858). Before 1858, Yorkshire probate was handled by ecclesiastical courts (the Prerogative and Exchequer Courts of York); external_links_search returned the Borthwick Institute for Archives, University of York (https://www.york.ac.uk/borthwick/) and Ancestry's "Yorkshire, England, Probate Records, 1521-1858" (collection 5246) and "York Peculiars Probate Index 1383-1883" (findmypast) as relevant holdings.
- **Where held:** Borthwick Institute for Archives, University of York (per external_links_search).

### Land records
- **Types:** Land tax assessments and estate rentals exist for West Yorkshire specifically ("West Yorkshire, England, Select Land Tax Records, 1704-1932", Ancestry collection 5108; "West Yorkshire, England Estate Rentals, 1380-1932", collection 9012) - not confirmed countywide.
- **Where held:** Ancestry (externally linked); FamilySearch Wiki Land and Property page was not fetched in this run.

### Military records
- Not a primary record type for a civilian death inquiry in this period; not surveyed in depth here.

### Cemetery records
- Monumental inscriptions: "Yorkshire Monumental Inscriptions" (findmypast, per external_links_search). No FindAGrave/BillionGraves-specific Yorkshire collection was returned by the tools in this run.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** The "Yorkshire Gazette" (findmypast, 1819-1920) spans 1851 and may carry a death notice or obituary. Other findmypast Yorkshire newspaper titles returned by external_links_search (e.g. Yorkshire Evening Post, Yorkshire Factory Times) start after 1851 and are not useful for this specific year.
- **Where held:** findmypast (https://www.findmypast.com/newspapers/england/yorkshire-gazette).

### Immigration/emigration records
- Not geographically central to an inland Yorkshire death in 1851; not surveyed in depth here.

### Tax records
- West Yorkshire-specific: "West Yorkshire, England, Electoral Registers, 1840-1962" (Ancestry 3057); "West Yorkshire, England, Select Rate Books, Accounts and Censuses, 1705-1893" (Ancestry 9016). These can substitute for missing vital records by placing a person in a given year.

### Other record types
- Workhouse, prison, and police records exist for West Yorkshire specifically (Ancestry collections 5085, 5105) and may be relevant if the death occurred in an institutional setting (e.g. workhouse infirmary).

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | England and Wales Census 1851 (id 2563939); England and Wales Death Registration Index 1837-2007 (id 2285341); England, Yorkshire, Parish Registers 1538-2016 (id 4439317); England, Yorkshire, Bishop's Transcripts 1547-1957 (id 4319956) | Civil death index and church burial corroboration | Free |
| FreeBMD | GRO birth/marriage/death index search (https://www.freebmd.org.uk/search) | Free alternative civil registration index | Free |
| Ancestry | Yorkshire, England, Probate Records, 1521-1858 (collection 5246); West/North Yorkshire Church of England Deaths and Burials collections | Pre-1858 probate; parish burial detail | Subscription |
| findmypast | Yorkshire Gazette newspaper archive; Yorkshire Burials; York Peculiars Probate Index 1383-1883 | Newspaper notice; burial index; pre-1858 probate index | Subscription |
| GENUKI | Yorkshire county page (http://www.genuki.org.uk/big/eng/YKS) | Finding-aid / parish directory | Free |
| Yorkshire BMD | https://www.yorkshirebmd.org.uk/ | Regional BMD index | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** volume_search and catalog_search returned no matching volumes or catalog entries for this standardPlace in this run, so no digitized-volume browse list or microfilm/catalog holdings could be detailed here; this is a tooling/coverage gap, not evidence the records do not exist in the FamilySearch Catalog.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Borthwick Institute for Archives, University of York | Ecclesiastical probate records (Prerogative and Exchequer Courts of York), parish records deposits | In-person / written request (per https://www.york.ac.uk/borthwick/) |
| General Register Office | Original civil registration certificates (births, marriages, deaths) | Certificate order by post/online |
| Exploring York archives | Local archives and local history holdings | Per https://exploreyork.org.uk/archives/ |

## Records NOT online
- The underlying GRO death certificate text (cause of death, informant, exact address) is never online - only the index is; the certificate must be ordered from the GRO.
- Pre-1858 Yorkshire probate case papers at the Borthwick Institute are a physical archive; only an index (York Peculiars Probate Index) was identified online in this run.

## Known record losses
- No record loss specific to Yorkshire or to 1851 was stated by any tool result in this run; none is reported here.

## Research tips
- Search the national GRO civil death index (via FreeBMD or FamilySearch) by surname and 1851 quarter/year first, since death registration was already compulsory nationally by this date per the 1837-2007 date range of the FamilySearch death index collection (id 2285341).
- Cross-check a GRO index match against the 1851 England and Wales census (collection 2563939) taken in March 1851, which can confirm the household shortly before a death later that year or show the person already absent if the death was early in the year.
- Search both county-wide "Yorkshire" collections and Riding-specific "West Yorkshire"/"North Yorkshire" collections - the same record may be catalogued under either label.
- If no civil registration match is found, check Church of England burial registers (FamilySearch's Yorkshire Parish Registers and Bishop's Transcripts collections, or Ancestry's West/North Yorkshire Deaths and Burials collections) for a corroborating burial entry.
- Check the Yorkshire Gazette (1819-1920, findmypast) for a death notice or obituary, especially if the family had any local prominence.
- If a will or administration may exist, search the pre-1858 ecclesiastical probate index (York Peculiars Probate Index, findmypast) rather than the National Index of Wills and Administrations, which only starts in 1858.

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.rationale: The guide correctly identifies civil death registration as the primary source and names FamilySearch collection 2285341 ('England and Wales, Death Registration Index 1837-2007') by exact title. It correctly cites Yorkshire BMD (http://www.yorkshirebmd.org.uk/) as a regional index. However, the guide contains a significant unsupported claim: it states that 'Yorkshire's records are frequently filed under its old sub-regions (West Yorkshire, North Yorkshire) rather than under "Yorkshire" as a whole' in the text response, but this claim does not appear in any tool response and is presented as established fact without attribution. The guide also claims 'wills from that era, held at the Borthwick Institute in York, exist only as physical archives rather than online' — while the Borthwick Institute is correctly cited from external_links_search, the claim about online availability is not grounded in tool output. The persisted guide_markdown correctly cites collection 2285341 and includes Yorkshire BMD, meeting the core test requirements, but the text response contains unsupported assertions about record filing practices.

dimensions.name: Completeness

The persisted locality guide includes specific collection IDs, date ranges, repositories, and research tips. The response covered the user's question about what records exist and where to search for a 1851 Yorkshire death.

dimensions.name: Jurisdiction accuracy
dimensions.rationale: The guide correctly identifies Yorkshire's historical structure and jurisdictional representation. It notes that place_search returned two representations: 'Yorkshire, England' (866-1801) and 'Yorkshire, England, United Kingdom' (1801-present), accurately reflecting the historical boundary. It correctly identifies the three Ridings (North, East, West) as the historical administrative division and notes that many collections are filed by Riding rather than county-wide. For 1851, the guide correctly uses the post-1801 representation. The jurisdictional context is accurate for the target time period.

dimensions.name: Record availability
dimensions.rationale: The guide identifies specific record classes with start dates and repositories: civil death registration (FamilySearch 2285341, 1837-2007, indexed online via FreeBMD and FamilySearch); church burials (FamilySearch 4439317 and 4319956, 1538-2016 and 1547-1957, indexed online); 1851 census (FamilySearch 2563939, indexed online); pre-1858 probate (Borthwick Institute, physical archive; York Peculiars Probate Index online via findmypast); and newspaper records (Yorkshire Gazette, findmypast, 1819-1920). It distinguishes indexed/imaged collections from physical archives requiring onsite research. Repositories are named (FamilySearch, FreeBMD, Ancestry, findmypast, Borthwick Institute, General Register Office). The guide correctly notes that the GRO certificate itself is never online and must be ordered.

dimensions.name: Research strategy
dimensions.rationale: The guide provides actionable search order: start with the national GRO civil death index (via FreeBMD or FamilySearch collection 2285341) because it is indexed and free; cross-check against the 1851 census (collection 2563939); search both county-wide and Riding-specific collections (West/North Yorkshire); if no civil match, check Church of England burial registers (FamilySearch Yorkshire Parish Registers and Bishop's Transcripts); check Yorkshire Gazette for death notices; search pre-1858 ecclesiastical probate index (York Peculiars) rather than the 1858+ national index. It includes specific FamilySearch collection IDs (2285341, 2563939, 4439317, 4319956), external links (FreeBMD, Yorkshire BMD, Borthwick Institute), and pitfalls: the Ridings filing quirk, the fact that civil index gives no cause of death (certificate required), the 1858 probate system boundary, and the need to order GRO certificates. Strategy is specific and grounded in tool results.
